key_insight: An open-source hardware-software toolkit automates RHEED control and analysis so both humans and AI agents can guide thin-film growth in a more autonomous way.
engineering_relevance: The toolkit lowers the barrier to integrating RHEED into closed-loop synthesis workflows by enabling programmable optics, automated alignment, and agent-accessible quantitative analysis.
method: Programmable electron-optics control on a pulsed laser deposition system
Automated beam alignment, rocking-curve acquisition, and training-free crystallographic azimuthal alignment
Shared GUI + programmatic interfaces, including an MCP server and extensible adapters for AI analysis/simulation
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a demonstration on a pulsed laser deposition system where natural-language requests successfully guided selection, configuration, and execution of RHEED analyses.
watch_item: Performance will still depend on instrument-specific integration and on the reliability of newly added community adapters or agent-driven workflows.
paper_title: An Open-Source Hardware and Software Toolkit to Enable Agentic RHEED-Guided Thin-Film Synthesis
